title: Thanksgiving Desserts
excerpt: Find easy Thanksgiving desserts for pumpkin pie, pumpkin roll, bread, muffins, and dump cake, gathered in one Grandma Recipe guide.
featuredImageAlt: Thanksgiving desserts with pumpkin pie, pumpkin roll, muffins, and bread
contentHtml:
After the turkey and gravy, thanksgiving desserts bring the table back to warm spice and whipped cream. This guide gathers Grandma Recipe’s best holiday sweets, from classic pumpkin pie to rolls, breads, muffins, and easy dump cake, so dessert feels planned instead of rushed.

Use this page as your dessert shortlist. Each recipe uses familiar pantry ingredients and clear steps for a full dessert table, a single centerpiece pie, or bake-ahead treats for guests.

How to Use This Thanksgiving Desserts Guide

Start with the kind of dessert you need:

  • Want the classic centerpiece? Bake pumpkin pie the day before so it sets overnight.
  • Need a pretty sliceable cake? Pumpkin roll looks special without fussy frosting work.
  • Baking for breakfast leftovers? Pumpkin bread and muffins travel well the next morning.
  • Short on time? Pumpkin dump cake or poke cake keeps dessert warm and simple.

If you only make one dessert, start with Classic Homemade Pumpkin Pie. For the full holiday menu, return to Easy Thanksgiving Recipes and Thanksgiving Side Dishes.

Pie comes first below, then cakes and rolls, then breads and muffins, with make-ahead tips before the FAQs.

Classic Pumpkin Pie

The dessert most people expect on a Thanksgiving table.

  • Classic Homemade Pumpkin Pie, classic homemade pumpkin pie with a creamy spiced filling and flaky crust.

Pumpkin Cakes and Rolls

Soft cakes for a second dessert tray or a smaller celebration.

  • Classic Pumpkin Roll, pumpkin roll with cream cheese filling and a dusting of powdered sugar.
  • Pumpkin Poke Cake, pumpkin poke cake with a creamy soak and soft crumb.
  • Pumpkin Dump Cake, easy pumpkin dump cake when you want dessert without mixing fuss.

Pumpkin Breads and Muffins

Bake-ahead loaves and muffins for Thanksgiving week breakfasts and neighbor gifts.

  • Grandma's Moist Pumpkin Bread, moist pumpkin bread with warm spices.
  • Soft Bakery-Style Pumpkin Muffins, bakery-style pumpkin muffins with a cinnamon-sugar sparkle.

Make-Ahead Dessert Tips

A few steady habits keep Thanksgiving desserts calm:

  • Bake pie the day before so the filling sets cleanly before slicing.
  • Cool cakes fully before rolling or frosting so layers stay neat.
  • Wrap breads and muffins airtight so they stay moist overnight.
  • Whip cream just before serving for the freshest finish on pie.
  • Keep one easy backup like dump cake if oven space is tight on turkey day.

FAQs

What is the best Thanksgiving dessert to make first?

Start with Classic Homemade Pumpkin Pie. It is the classic finish and holds beautifully overnight in the fridge.

Can I make Thanksgiving desserts ahead?

Yes. Classic Homemade Pumpkin Pie, Grandma's Moist Pumpkin Bread, and Soft Bakery-Style Pumpkin Muffins all keep well. Pumpkin roll chills nicely once filled. Dump cake is best warm from the oven.

What if I do not want to make pie crust?

Choose Pumpkin Dump Cake or Pumpkin Poke Cake for a pumpkin dessert without rolling dough, or bake Grandma's Moist Pumpkin Bread for a simpler sweet finish.

How many Thanksgiving desserts do I need?

One centerpiece pie is enough for most tables. Add pumpkin roll or muffins if you want a second option for kids or overnight guests.

What dessert pairs well with a full turkey dinner?

Classic Homemade Pumpkin Pie is the classic match. If dinner already feels heavy, serve smaller slices of pie beside Soft Bakery-Style Pumpkin Muffins for a lighter second tray.

Final Thoughts

Good thanksgiving desserts do not need a bakery counter of options. Pick one pumpkin pie, maybe one cake or bread, and let whipped cream do the rest. Bookmark this guide, bake what fits your timeline, and return to Easy Thanksgiving Recipes when you are ready to finish turkey and sides.
